name: Make sound and timely decisions
definition: The leader must be able to rapidly estimate a situation and make a sound decision based on that estimation. Hesitation or reluctance to make a decision leads subordinates to lose confidence in your abilities as a leader.

rows.situation: When you have to choose a path
rows.under: Picks from habit, or from whoever spoke last, without a real estimate.
rows.justRight: Takes a fast, honest read of the facts you have, then chooses.
rows.over: Builds a perfect picture of the situation and the window closes.

rows.situation: When the remaining facts would take too long
rows.under: Waits for a complete file and the team sits still.
rows.justRight: Decides on what you have, says what you assumed, and watches for the fact that would change it.
rows.over: Decides on a hunch and treats later facts as an insult.

rows.situation: When the team is waiting on your call
rows.under: Delays until they lose confidence and start guessing.
rows.justRight: Makes the call as soon as you have enough to be sound, and says it clearly.
rows.over: Snaps a call so you look decisive, then spends the week undoing it.

rows.situation: When the decision you made is wrong
rows.under: Bluffs through it so you do not look indecisive.
rows.justRight: Revises it as soon as you know, and tells the people who are already moving.
rows.over: Revises so often that nobody trusts the current call.

rows.situation: When a little more time would change the quality of the call
rows.under: Treats every wait as weakness and forces a thin call.
rows.justRight: Takes the time when the wait is cheap and the extra fact is real, then decides.
rows.over: Uses one more input as a habit, including on calls that will not get better.

rows.situation: When people can already see the call is thin
rows.under: Pretends certainty you do not have.
rows.justRight: Names the weak spot, keeps or changes the call, and does not bluff.
rows.over: Walks back a sound call because someone looked doubtful.
